patch.objective: Troubleshooting connectivity issues: DNS failures, asymmetric routing, duplicate IP/MAC addresses, DHCP issues, IPSec and BGP problems, and routing loops

sources.cite: CompTIA CloudNetX CNX-001 V1 Exam Objectives, document version 5.0: Network Architecture Design 31%, Network Security 28%, Operations, Monitoring and Performance 16%, Network Troubleshooting 25%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 1.4 'Given a scenario, analyze availability requirements to recommend technologies that meet business needs' (load balancing); 2.3 'Given a scenario, configure the appropriate access controls to secure a network' (firewall rules, network security groups); 'Explain the troubleshooting methodology'; 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot connectivity issues' (DNS issues). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-16. Relevant text: dns=default, 'NetworkManager will update /etc/resolv.conf to reflect the nameservers provided by currently active connections'; rc-manager is 'about how NetworkManager writes to /etc/resolv.conf, if at all', and with a regular file NetworkManager writes it directly. That a hand edit is replaced the next time the connection is reactivated is the author's reading of that behavior.

Fictional hosts and addresses: the private range 10.0.5.0/24, the documentation range 203.0.113.0/24 (IETF RFC 5737) and the reserved .example names (IETF RFC 2606). Command output is an authored rendering of ip, ping, traceroute, ss, dig and nmcli output, shortened.
